en: The Jātaka:
The Fifth Collection, Chapter on the Jeweled Earrings (Maṇikuṇḍalavagga)
1. The Maṇikuṇḍala Jātaka “I have lost my chariot and my jeweled earrings;
likewise, I have lost my children and my wife.”
"All wealth has been exhausted without remainder;
why do you not find comfort in this time of sorrow?
"Beforehand, O mortal, wealth abandons you."
Either Macca will abandon you first;
for those who possess wealth and pursue their desires are impermanent.
Therefore, I do not grieve at a time of sorrow.
The moon rises and waxes full;
the sun, having shone its heat, sets.
These worldly conditions, O Sattuka, have been understood by me.
Therefore, I do not grieve at a time for grieving.
“A lazy householder who indulges in sensual pleasures is not good;
one who has gone forth but is unrestrained is not good.
It is not good for a king to act without reflection;
it is not good for one who is wise yet prone to anger.
A noble should act with careful consideration.
“Not by lack of reflection does one become a lord of the earth; O King,
for one who acts with reflection, glory and fame increase.”
The Maṇikuṇḍala Jātaka is the first.
